officialDocsConsulted.summary: The Model aliases table confirms the issue AC's nine-alias set verbatim, including 'best' ('Uses Fable 5 where your organization has access to it, otherwise the latest Opus model'): default, best, fable, sonnet, opus, haiku, sonnet[1m], opus[1m], opusplan. The same page ALSO documents 'opusplan[1m]' as a settable model value ('To force 1M context for both phases when you are not on an auto-upgrade tier, set the model to opusplan[1m]'), which the issue's nine-item list omits; because the claude guard is fail-closed, an omitted-but-valid alias would turn a working operator config into a blocked dispatch, so this PRD's canonical set is the doc's superset (ten values). Full model names (claude-*) remain valid alongside aliases.
officialDocsConsulted.localConventionConflict: MODEL_OPTIONS (src/ui/ConfigScreen.tsx:98-107) and CONTEXT.md's 'model tier alias' term both list only 8 aliases (no 'best', no 'opusplan[1m]'); this PRD resolves the clash by putting the doc-verified superset in a NEW non-UI module plus a MODEL_OPTIONS-containment test, and by updating the CONTEXT.md term, while leaving the out-of-scope picker untouched.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: A positional argument to `bun test` is a filename FILTER, not a path, unless it starts with './' or '/' ('To run a specific file in the test runner, make sure the path starts with ./ or /'), and a filter that matches zero test files exits non-zero. Every named-command oracle in this PRD therefore uses the explicit './test/...' form (a bare 'test/supervisor/plan-runner.test.ts' filter was measured to fuzzy-match a DIFFERENT file on main), and the red-on-main sweep of not-yet-existing test files relies on that documented non-zero exit.

userStories.title: Review round 1 fix 001: address reviewer finding
userStories.notes: WARNING [src/commands/run.ts:811]: The new orchestrator model-resolution abort is surfaced to the operator under the hardcoded headline 'codex auth preflight failed'. setupPanes returns { blocked: true, message: 'model-resolution-failed: ...' } (run.ts:492-494), and runRun prints it via printError('codex auth preflight failed', result.blocked) (run.ts:811), so a config/model-pin failure renders as '✗ codex auth preflight failed — model-resolution-failed: no valid codex model pin for phase ...'. The bold headline is factually wrong (auth is fine) and points the operator at `codex login` instead of project.toml. The diff defends the reuse on cost grounds (scripts/cam/patterns.md US-007 bullet: 'reuses that exact same surfacing path for free, no new escalation plumbing needed'), which is not a valid rationale for a misleading operator diagnostic on a fail-closed path. Mechanical fix: carry a header/kind alongside the blocked message (or branch the printError headline on the 'model-resolution-failed:' prefix) and assert it in test/commands/run-model-resolution.test.ts.

userStories.title: Add the backend-aware model resolution layer with fail-closed codex and claude paths
userStories.description: As a cam phase dispatch, I need one resolution function that turns (phase, backend) into either a concrete dispatchable model or an actionable abort, so that a codex dispatch never receives a claude alias and a mistyped claude model never reaches spawn.
acceptanceCriteria: A new module src/config/model-resolution.ts exports resolvePhaseModel({ phase, backend, configPath?, cacheReader? }) returning a discriminated { ok: true, model } | { ok: false, message }, and for the codex backend applies exactly this precedence: nested [models.codex].<phase> pin (verbatim, highest) > non-claude-shaped flat [models].<phase> value > cache auto-resolution > fail-closed abort. RED-ON-MAIN (swept 2026-07-23: exit 1, no matching test file). [oracle: bun test ./test/config/model-resolution.test.ts]

The single decision fn for 'is this flat value claude-shaped' on the codex path is the US-001 SUPERSET isClaudeAliasModel imported from src/supervisor/codex-auth.ts (matching the existing codexAuthPreflight guard); validateClaudeModel is imported only for the claude-backend typo-guard, and no third notion of claude-shaped is defined in this module. RED-ON-MAIN (swept 2026-07-23: exit 2, src/config/model-resolution.ts does not exist, so grep exits 2). [oracle: grep -q 'isClaudeAliasModel' src/config/model-resolution.ts]

A dashed non-prefixed flat value is governed by that superset: with backend=codex, no nested pin, and flat [models].implementer = 'sonnet-4-5', resolution does NOT honor it as a pin: with an injected cache reader that resolves it returns the cache's top slug, and with a not-ok cache reader it returns ok:false. A non-claude-shaped flat value IS a valid codex pin: with backend=codex and flat [models].implementer = 'gpt-5-codex', resolution returns 'gpt-5-codex' verbatim and the injected cache reader is never invoked (asserted with a reader that records invocation and would otherwise return a different slug). For the claude backend, resolution returns the configured value verbatim for 'opus', 'sonnet', 'best', 'opusplan[1m]' and 'claude-opus-4-8', and returns ok:false with a message naming the offending value and the project.toml [models] key for 'sonnett' and 'gpt-5.6-sol'; the codex cache reader is never invoked on the claude path. findings.text: The new orchestrator model-resolution abort is surfaced to the operator under the hardcoded headline 'codex auth preflight failed'. setupPanes returns { blocked: true, message: 'model-resolution-failed: ...' } (run.ts:492-494), and runRun prints it via printError('codex auth preflight failed', result.blocked) (run.ts:811), so a config/model-pin failure renders as '✗ codex auth preflight failed — model-resolution-failed: no valid codex model pin for phase ...'. The bold headline is factually wrong (auth is fine) and points the operator at `codex login` instead of project.toml. The diff defends the reuse on cost grounds (scripts/cam/patterns.md US-007 bullet: 'reuses that exact same surfacing path for free, no new escalation plumbing needed'), which is not a valid rationale for a misleading operator diagnostic on a fail-closed path. Mechanical fix: carry a header/kind alongside the blocked message (or branch the printError headline on the 'model-resolution-failed:' prefix) and assert it in test/commands/run-model-resolution.test.ts.

(consider-class, non-blocking) validateClaudeModel accepts only exact CLAUDE_MODEL_ALIASES membership or a /^claude-/ full name, so it fail-closes the other model-name forms the same consulted doc documents as valid for the `model` setting (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config, 'Available models': Amazon Bedrock inference profile ARN, Microsoft Foundry deployment name, Google Cloud Agent Platform version name). cam's posture is subscription-only (docs/adr/0028, src/orchestrator/context-window.ts), so this is not reachable today, but the PRD used exactly this argument to add opusplan[1m] ('an omitted-but-valid alias would turn a working operator config into a blocked dispatch'). Consider an escape hatch or a documented note; a design call, not a mechanical fix.

resolveCodexModel discriminates 'nested [models.codex].<phase> pin fired' from 'flat value' by string inequality (withNested !== flatOnly). When an operator sets the SAME value in both tables (e.g. [models] implementer = "opus" and [models.codex] implementer = "opus"), nestedPinFired is false and the documented rule-1 'nested pin returned verbatim, no claude-shape check' silently does not apply: the explicit pin falls through to cache auto-resolution. Benign today (a claude alias is not dispatchable on codex anyway), but the precedence is heuristic rather than exact, and no test covers the equal-values case. A targeted read of [models.codex].<phase> would make it exact.

The planner/auditor model-resolution aborts return modelResolution.message unprefixed under kind 'codex-auth-failed' (plan-runner.ts:1026/1047), while the three sibling sites (loop.ts:1124, review.ts:411, run.ts:493) all prefix with 'model-resolution-failed: '. Adding the same prefix here keeps a model-resolution abort distinguishable from a real auth failure wherever the reason surfaces (escalation mail, event log), without touching the PlanPhaseResult union the AC pinned.

In the parametrized rejection loop, the bad = '' case asserts expect(result.message).toContain(bad), which is vacuously true for the empty string. The companion expect(result.ok).toBe(false) still makes the case meaningful, but the message assertion for '' proves nothing; consider asserting a stable substring of the guard message instead for that one input.

Section (z) documents the codex fail-closed abort, but not the other new operator-facing abort this PR introduces: the strict claude typo-guard ('<value>' is not a recognized claude model ...; check the project.toml [models].<phase> key), which now hard-blocks every claude-backed dispatch for a non-alias, non-claude-* model value. A two-line addition to the same section would cover it.
